items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Next, was the group of Mackenzie... Mackenzie was also playing flute and was willing to help as much as possible. I decided to use those guys...

ctx.x: He said that if the American Cultural Center really wanted to do something cultural for his country and the people, they should send a couple of American music professors to teach the young students and musicians, the different arts of America, and the right approach to the form of jazz that was known in American, and other parts of the continent.

The director of 'The Sun' had come to the rehearsals also with a young musician in his early thirties who was a trumpet player from Ghana. His name was Mackenzie. He knew quite a lot about jazz and was a quiet/nice person. He told me that he had seen the director of the Cultural Center the previous week and told him that this band would be incapable to accompany me. He had offered to form a little group and make them rehears, but they had declined his offer.

We asked him if he could contact some better musicians. Unfortunately he said, two were out of town, but he knew a lead guitar and a guitarist and also a drummer. The assistant director,who by then was getting very worried said that he was going with him and we went back to our hotel and waited and waited.
